title: Top Stories: iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate Out Now, Siri AI Waitlist, and More
content:
All of Apple's products introduced at last week's event with the exception of the iPhone Duo are now available, with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 all launching on Friday.


While new hardware is always a welcome arrival, users of existing hardware also got big upgrades this week with the releases of iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate and more. Apple is also already looking ahead to iOS 27.1 that will ship with the iPhone Duo next month and iOS 27.2 that will see the first significant round of improvements to iOS 27 for all users, so read on below for all of details on these stories and more!

Top Stories

Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 With Siri AI and Liquid Glass Update

Following last week's big iPhone event, this week saw the traditional public release of Apple's new major operating system updates, headlined by iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.


iOS 27 brings new Siri AI capabilities to users in many countries around the world, as well as a variety of other new features and improvements. For a quick introduction to iOS 27, check out our list of 10 features to try first, and when you're ready for more, move on to our look at 50 new things your iPhone can do in iOS 27.

iOS 27 Ultimate Mega Guide links to all of the feature coverage we've been putting together for the release.

macOS Golden Gate Now Available With Siri AI, Visual Intelligence and More

On the Mac side, this week saw the release of macOS Golden Gate 27. The update introduces Siri AI, a smarter chatbot version of ‌Siri‌ with a dedicated ‌Siri‌ app. It also brings Visual Intelligence to the Mac for the first time, and tweaks the look of the Liquid Glass design update Apple introduced last year.


For a quick overview of what's new in macOS Golden Gate, be sure to check out our list of 10 features to try first, including Siri AI, easier creation of Shortcuts and Safari Extensions, performance improvements, and more, and then move on to our guide to 50 new features and changes for a more in-depth look.

Apple Says iPhone 18 Pro Max Sold in U.S. Differs in One Way

Following last week's introduction of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, there was some confusion over the cellular modems included in the devices, with it appearing that Apple's own C2 modem was only included in the iPhone 18 Pro.


Apple later updated its spec pages for the new models around the world, making it clear that the C2 is included in both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in every country around the world EXCEPT for the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the United States. That device continues to use the Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem from the iPhone 17 Pro models, but Apple has yet to explain the reason for this difference.

Reminder: iOS 27's All-New Siri AI Has a Waitlist, Here's How to Sign Up

If you recently installed iOS 27 on your iPhone, you might be wondering where the new-and-improved Siri AI and dedicated Siri app are. In case you missed it, you must join Apple's waitlist in order to gain access to these new features.


Keep in mind that while iOS 27 is compatible with the iPhone 11 and newer, Siri AI is limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer. It is also not currently available at all in EU countries due to Apple's regulatory battle with the European Commission over Digital Markets Act requirements.

For those who are eligible for Siri AI, joining the waitlist is a simple process in the Settings app. Once on the list, wait times seem to vary, with some users receiving access to Siri AI within a few minutes of signing up and others having to wait a few hours or even days.

Apple Releases First iOS 27.2 Beta

With iOS 27.0 out the door, Apple this week seeded the first beta of iOS 27.2 and related updates to developers for testing purposes. Yes, that's right...iOS 27.2, not 27.1.


The biggest change in the first iOS 27.2 beta is the revamped Health app that Apple showed off at last week's iPhone event, although Apple says it won't be included in the public release of the update, so the general public will need to wait a bit longer for it to be available. For more, check out our full list of everything new in the first beta of iOS 27.2.

iCloud+ Now Includes Apple TV, Apple Arcade, and Curated Apple Music Stations in Over 100 Countries

Apple this week announced a new subscription initiative that turns paid iCloud+ subscriptions into a broader services bundle in more than 100 countries.


In select countries, Apple says every paid iCloud+ plan, including the cheapest 50GB tier, now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade "at no additional cost," while family sharing extends the storage, TV and Arcade access to up to five people.

The initiative does not include the U.S., Canada, Australia, nor is it offered in the UK and other European markets, but it is clearly more than a promotional offer, since Apple TV and Apple Arcade will stop being sold as individual subscriptions through Apple in countries where it has launched.

title: Apple Exec Says 'Hold Us Accountable' on iPhone Duo Crease
content:
Apple hardware engineering VP Tom Marieb spoke with TechRadar and shared some candid thoughts about Apple's upcoming iPhone Duo.


The ‌iPhone Duo‌ uses a matte nano-texture display, which is meant to cut down on glare and minimize the visibility of the crease. When asked if the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s crease would be more visible over time, as that's what tends to happen on other foldables, Marieb said the nano-texture display would help. He asked people to hold the company "accountable" on crease visibility.
Hold us accountable to that, please. The choice of a matte finish — apart from it being beautiful — is part of that equation. When you look at glossy displays, their specularity makes it very easy to pick up topology differences. That's part of the reason we picked the matte finish — it's not only beautiful in terms of preventing glare, but it's also more forgiving of [hinge] changes over time.

Marieb said the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s hinge was something he was "especially proud of" because it took a long time to get the right design. Apple wanted a durable hinge that felt solid to open and close.
We really worked on the torque profile very heavily, and that means changing a lot of the mechanical properties of the hinge to have it feel solid, like a high-end automobile's car door, when you shut it. That was design intent, so people would have a feeling like, 'Oh, it's okay. This is well crafted, and it's safe for me to use and not worry about it.'

Apple didn't want the hinge to be "floppy," so torque had to be perfected for different use cases. The hinge Apple came up with lets the ‌iPhone Duo‌ be used in partially folded seated and standing modes, as well as open and closed. Marieb said "a lot of blood, sweat, and tears" went into the hinge design.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has a battery capacity over 20 watt-hours, which means there are additional shipping requirements. If an ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max needs to be shipped somewhere, its maximum battery capacity has to be limited through firmware.


According to Apple, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max uses an "innovative battery-firmware solution" that limits battery capacity to below 20Wh between when the iPhone is manufactured and its delivery to a customer. Activating the iPhone removes the limit to make the battery's full charging capacity available. iPhones that are not yet activated or still in the box will not need Prepare to Ship because they are already limited to under 20Wh.

Customers who need to ship the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max for repair, trade-in, or other purposes have to use a new Prepare to Ship feature. Prepare to Ship discharges the battery to below 20Wh and sets a charge limit so the iPhone stays below the threshold during the shipping process.

The Prepare to Ship option can be accessed by going to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Prepare to Ship. Apple warns that the iPhone can become "warmer than usual" during Prepare to Ship if the battery needs to be discharged. When finished, the iPhone shows a "Ready to Ship" status in Settings.

If Prepare to Ship needs to be undone, there is an option in the same section of the Settings app to undo the shipping preparation. Depending on the reason the user selected for the Prepare to Ship feature, there could be a 14-day waiting period before it can be disabled.

title: Hands-On With the Apple Watch Series 12
content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 came out today, and we picked one up to get a look at the new feature set. There are no major external changes, but Apple updated the device's internals and health sensors.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

The Apple Watch Series 12 has the same design as the Series 11, but it does come in different colors. The aluminum models are available in a light gold shade that's distinct from the rose gold Apple used last year, as well as dark bronze, black, and space gray. There are also ceramic models in pearl white and night blue, and polished titanium models in radiant gold and natural. On the aluminum models, Apple is now using Ceramic Shield 2 instead of Ion-X glass, and the new material is 60 percent tougher.

You might not be able to tell a Series 11 apart from a Series 12 when looking at the front, but the back has been updated. Apple says the upgraded sensors make the Apple Watch Series 12 the most accurate wearable for heart rate sensing.

The Series 12 has a Health Sensing System that pairs the new sensors with an S11 chip that's faster than the S10 in the prior-generation model. It takes heart rate readings every five seconds now and measures heart rate variability as often as every five minutes.

It's early, but so far we haven't seen the higher sampling rates cause excessive battery drain. The Apple Watch Series 12 is still rated for all-day battery life, and charging is faster this year. You can get up to 12 hours of normal usage from a 15-minute charge, but you need to use the Apple Watch charger that comes with the Series 12. Older chargers won't give you the faster charging rate.

The Health Sensing System powers a readiness score that lets you know whether to go all-out on activity or take a rest day. It's based on metrics such as recent activity, vitals, and sleep, and will adjust as the day continues. It takes about a week of data collection from the Series 12 before you start getting a readiness score.

Live Rewind and Siri Recap features, but those won't be available until later this year.

Even though the Apple Watch hasn't seen a design refresh, the health features make this a decent update. You may not want to upgrade if you have the Series 10 or Series 11, but anything older is worth upgrading from.

title: A US NAND factory could reshape storage supply, but not yet for Apple
content:
SK Hynix-owned Solidigm is considering a U.S. factory for the storage chips used in phones, computers, and data centers, a move that would reduce its dependence on China as Washington pressures foreign chipmakers to manufacture in America.

Upstate New York has emerged as the leading candidate, Reuters reported Friday, citing three people familiar with the discussions. No agreement has been reached, and the location, investment, capacity, and construction schedule remain undecided.
Solidigm said it regularly evaluates options to improve its long-term competitiveness but hasn't chosen a course of action. SK Hynix similarly confirmed that it is reviewing options without committing to the factory.
The proposed project would be separate from SK Hynix's discussions about producing memory chips at Intel's planned Ohio facility.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Ultra 4 Buyer's Guide
content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 bring new health sensors, a new chip, and more detailed recovery insights to Apple's smartwatch lineup, so how do they compare?


Both models feature the S11 chip, 4GB of RAM, 64GB of storage, and the new Health Sensing System, which measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day. They also share Readiness, Recovery HRV, daytime vitals, improved step tracking, hypertension notifications, sleep apnea notifications, Sleep Score, and more. This means that the Ultra 4's higher price does not buy you more advanced everyday health tracking.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799. The gap narrows if you want a premium case material, with the titanium Series 12 starting at $699. This year, the Series 12 also gains a ceramic option starting at $899, making it more expensive than the Ultra despite its smaller size and shorter battery life.

The Apple Watch Ultra continues to focus on durability, extended battery life, and additional capabilities for activities like diving and exploration. Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two Apple Watches is best for you. For most users, the Apple Watch Series 12 is the better choice. It offers the same performance, health sensors, Readiness insights, and Audio Intelligence features as the Ultra 4 in a thinner, lighter device. The aluminum model delivers these benefits for $400 less, making it the stronger option for everyday use and regular workouts.

The Ultra 4's most broadly useful advantage is battery life. Its longer endurance makes overnight wear and extended workouts easier to fit around charging. You do not need to be an endurance athlete to appreciate less frequent charging, but the premium is easier to justify if the Series 12 cannot comfortably cover your usual activities and charging habits.

For hiking away from cellular coverage, recreational scuba diving, or very long events, the Ultra has a clearer purpose. Satellite communications, dual-frequency GPS, greater water resistance, and extended workout modes address needs that the Series 12 cannot fully meet. The Action button and brighter display may also appeal to enthusiasts who simply want more capable hardware.

Size and appearance remain substantial trade-offs. The Ultra is considerably bulkier and heavier despite offering a display only slightly larger than the 46mm Series 12's. The Series 12 is more discreet and offers polished titanium and ceramic finishes, making it better suited to buyers who prioritize comfort or appearance. Try on the Ultra before buying if you are unsure about its size.

title: MacRumors Giveaway: Win an iPhone Duo From iMazing
content:
For this week's giveaway we've teamed up with iMazing to offer MacRumors readers a chance to win an iPhone Duo and a copy of the iMazing software to go along with it.


If you're unfamiliar with iMazing, it's Mac and PC software that offers a speedy, simple way to manage all of the data on your iPhone. You can make backups, add and delete photos, videos, and music, save content like messages, and much more.

While Apple has the built-in Finder on Mac for managing an iPhone, iMazing has a ton of features Apple doesn't offer. You can set up automatic backups with snapshots that make it easy to find what you're looking for and selective restore for bringing back just what you need. A useful search tool lets you find files on your devices and in your backups.


There's a Device Overview with detailed information about your iPhone in one spot, and dedicated tools for browsing, exporting, and archiving content. You can transfer photos, music, books, movies, and other media files from your computer to your iPhone and vice versa. You can even create an entire archive of your messages from the Messages app or WhatsApp.

iMazing can be used for screen recording on macOS, and there are diagnostic and device-info export tools. A Spyware Analyzer lets you know if any of your devices have been compromised.


The software isn't limited to the iPhone. It works with the iPad and Vision Pro, along with older devices like the iPod. If you have an old iPod with music on it, you can use iMazing to get it off. It also supports song transfers from non-iOS music players.

iMazing was entirely overhauled in 2024, and since then, the software has continued to get regular updates to add new features. The user interface has been updated with a collapsible sidebar and customizable device and backup list views, and data export has been improved. You can export all of your data with advanced filters, and use the same filters on the Unified Logs browser. Business features have improved too, with streamlined MDM enrollment, a Command Line Interface for advanced interaction with iOS devices and backups, and the iMazing Profile Editor 2 for configuring macOS app, notification, and login permissions.


You'll never have to worry about a device being unsupported with iMazing. It's updated with ongoing support for new models as they come out. In the near future, iMazing plans to add Android support, which will make it even more useful. iMazing can be downloaded from the iMazing website at prices starting at $30. iMazing has personal subscriptions, family subscriptions, and enterprise subscriptions, with free trials available. Some functions are free without a purchase.


We have a 256GB ‌iPhone Duo‌ and a copy of iMazing to give away to one MacRumors reader. 10 other readers will win a copy of iMazing. Since the ‌iPhone Duo‌ has not been released yet, this is a prize that will be delivered after the device launches on October 23.

title: 'Shop Different': Apple Retail Pioneer Ron Johnson Shares the Inside Story
content:
Back in 1999, unhappy at how Macs were being positioned in traditional computer retail stores, Steve Jobs decided that Apple needed to make its own push into retail. The man he brought on to lead the initiative was Ron Johnson, previously the vice president of merchandising at Target.


Johnson and writer Zander Nethercutt have teamed up for a new book entitled Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple's Genius, releasing next Tuesday, September 22, and I recently had a chance to read through the book and chat with Johnson about it.

Shop Different covers Johnson's background including his time at department store Mervyn's and at Target, but the bulk of the book unsurprisingly focuses on his work at Apple as his biggest success story and a topic of significant interest for legions of Apple fans and others in the business world and beyond.

Johnson started at Apple on February 1, 2000, and he worked hand-in-hand with Jobs and other Apple executives to develop a vision and buildout plan for Apple retail stores, leading to the opening of the company's first two stores in May 2001.

Shop Different goes into detail on the trials and tribulations of developing the first stores and their weak early performance, struggles that ultimately gave way to the massive success that the stores have achieved.

Some of the high-level background of the Apple retail development process, including how Apple built out a full-scale store mockup in a Cupertino warehouse, has long been known, but Johnson dives into much more detail on how everything played out. Johnson describes early meetings with Jobs as they discussed the philosophy behind delving directly into retail, the challenges of securing prime real estate, Jobs' initial reaction to Johnson's proposed "Genius Bar" name for the stores' support services, and much more.  

Shop Different, Johnson shares some touching moments from his interactions with Jobs as pancreatic cancer took its toll on the Apple founder, as well as Johnson's transition to CEO of department store JCPenney, a difficult period amid Jobs' decline and death, misgivings about leaving Apple to take on the new role, and ultimately his inability to achieve success turning JCPenney's fortunes around.

You know, really, honestly, I do. I'm very impressed.

And part of it goes back to, when we launched the stores, Tim and Deirdre were involved on the operations side. I tell a story in the book where Steve said, you know, "What are the ten things you need to do well?" And one of those was inventory...inventory management. Well, Deirdre kind of led the team that managed the inventory. And so she was involved with the stores before we opened our first one.

Among the highlights for Johnson are Apple's ongoing focus on improving the quality, size, and locations of stores to reflect the caliber of the brand, rather than focusing on overall store count, and how Apple has maintained a high standard for its "exceptional" retail employees, some of whom have been with the company for many years.

You know, I was the first retailer at Apple. And I built the initial team and, we relied a lot on other Apple departments, but fundamentally, I think Tim felt that he's got to find a retail leader to run the stores, right?

And so he started out with an operations leader, but obviously that led to a pretty quick change, because the stores were never about, sure, it's important how you operate, but it's really about a culture of love and connection, and you've got to have someone who will embrace that, right?

And then you went to Angela, who was a highly respected retail leader. But I think after Angela left, which was nearing the 20th anniversary of the stores, he kind of concluded, I think, that maybe an internal person who really understands Apple could be a great leader of the stores.

She's been there from the beginning, so I think Tim made the decision to really make sure the stores were highly integrated, connected with Apple as a company. Because it's pretty easy for them to be on their own doing their own thing. But once you bring in someone like Deirdre, who has managed the People teams, has managed at Apple, has managed a lot of the operations teams at Apple, you'll get a different level of connectivity to Apple itself.

Johnson also had particularly kind words for Vanessa Trigub, who was named to a vice president role last year to head up retail operations under O'Brien, with Johnson calling her a "fabulous leader" who "has a great vision for how to serve customers."

iPhone Duo, but he acknowledged the rumors about the device and mentioned the role Apple retail will play in allowing customers to experience the new product category.
What a great opportunity when this new, supposedly foldable phone comes out. Now, I think the stores will be more crowded during September and October. They'll be more crowded than in years. Because, remember, one to two billion people that are on iPhones, that use them every day.



Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple's Genius is available for pre-order now through Amazon and other book retailers, and it launches on Tuesday, September 22.

title: The MacRumors Show: Is the iPhone Duo Actually Worth It?
content:
On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show, we revisit the iPhone Duo debate, early impressions of the AirPods 5, and the merits of Apple's latest iPhone and Apple Watch upgrades.

Subscribe to The MacRumors Show YouTube channel for more videos

Apple's first foldable iPhone continues to divide opinion, with much of the discussion centering on whether its larger inner display justifies the compromises elsewhere. Combining an iPhone and an iPad-like device has obvious appeal, but its value depends on how often that extra screen space would actually be used.

Watching videos, reading, referencing documents, and working across multiple apps could all make the foldable display worthwhile, particularly when traveling. For users who primarily take photos, send messages, and browse social media, the benefits may be harder to justify against the device's price, weight, thickness, and camera trade-offs. The excitement surrounding a new form factor also raises the question of whether buyers will embrace it for the long term or return to a conventional iPhone.

nano-texture finish introduces a balance between reducing glare and retaining the appearance of a glossy screen, with hands-on impressions offering a different perspective from photos and videos online. Other considerations include using the wider form factor one-handed, switching from Face ID to Touch ID, and potentially replacing an iPad on some trips.

Their fit and improved active noise cancellation could make them particularly appealing to users who struggle with AirPods Pro's silicone tips. We also consider the value of the higher-end model and how iOS 27's equalizer can help adjust a sound profile that may initially seem too bass-heavy.

Apple Watch Series 12 and redesigned Health app receive a closer look, with this year's health features forming a more substantial upgrade after several relatively modest generations. Clearer presentation of health data and new longevity information promise to make collected metrics more useful. Whether those additions justify replacing an older watch remains a separate question for owners whose basic fitness and sleep-tracking needs are already met.

iPhone 18 Pro's variable-aperture camera, smaller Dynamic Island, and new Photographic Styles. The discussion weighs how noticeable these changes will be in everyday use, with the new film-inspired styles potentially offering as much appeal as the camera hardware improvements. We also look at whether owners of recent Pro models have sufficient reason to switch, and when a discounted iPhone 17 Pro could offer better value.

title: Apple Designers Explain the Thinking Behind iPhone Duo
content:
Apple's design team reveals how notebooks helped inspire the iPhone Duo, along with interface principles and expectations for future features, in a new interview with GQ.


The interview features Apple CEO John Ternus, Vice President of Industrial Design Molly Anderson, and Vice President of Human Interface Design Steve Lemay. In addition to the device's previously announced features, Anderson and Lemay discuss how Apple approached its physical design and the experience of moving between its two displays.

Anderson said familiar notebooks provided a reference for making a device that offers more space while remaining compact enough to carry comfortably.

Everyone knows what a notebook feels like in the pocket and what it feels like to carry around. So that was a big part of the inspiration: 'How do you get to something that gives you space but also feels compact?'"


The ‌iPhone Duo‌'s proportions are derived from the international A-series paper system, allowing the device to retain the same proportions when opened and closed. 

Anderson also explained how Apple tuned the hinge's resistance. Its custom variable torque profile makes the device easy to open before biasing it toward remaining open and lying flat. 

Lemay said that the guiding idea of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s software was to make unfolding feel like expanding the device users were already holding. Maintaining the location and recognizability of controls was part of that approach, so users would not have to search again for a button after opening the phone. The transition animation was designed to reveal an inner display that appears to grow beneath the outer one.

It was really important to us from the beginning that iPhone Duo feels like one cohesive experience, not two different products awkwardly fused together.


iPad and existing iPhones. He characterized the result as the "greatest hits" of those products.

The interview also questioned how Apple expects the product to develop after launch. Lemay said developers will devise uses that Apple's design team has not anticipated, and suggested that some could influence the wider foldable industry and change the direction of the ‌iPhone Duo‌ itself in the future.

There are so many things the developers will come up with that we've never anticipated. Some of those will become big ideas that take over the industry and change the product in interesting ways.

title: Are iPhone 17 Pro Cases Compatible With iPhone 18 Pro? Here's What Apple Says
content:
Can you use iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max cases with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and vice versa?


Apple's official answer is no, according to Daring Fireball's John Gruber. Apple said the camera plateau on the iPhone 18 Pro models is ever so slightly thicker this year. Gruber said the difference is one-tenth of a millimeter: 11.5mm vs. 11.4mm. It is a minor difference, but Apple would obviously prefer to sell you a new case.

In practice, most cases should be interchangeable. In his personal testing, Gruber said his iPhone 17 Pro cases fit the iPhone 18 Pro models perfectly, as did iPhone 18 Pro cases on iPhone 17 Pro models. So, both generations of Apple-branded cases should work with both generations of iPhones, and many third-party cases should be fine too.

title: Best Apple Watch 2026: Series 12 vs Ultra 4 vs SE 3
content:
Macworld





Choosing the right Apple Watch depends on your budget, lifestyle and which features matter most to you. As of September 2026, Apple’s lineup consists of the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch SE 3, although the various combinations of case size, material, color and band can make choosing one seem like a bit of a minefield.
The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best choice for most people, combining a tougher display and more advanced heart-rate sensing with an S11 chip and 24-hour battery life. The larger and more rugged Apple Watch Ultra 4 is designed for endurance sports and outdoor adventures, offering precision GPS, diving features and up to 50 hours of battery life. The Apple Watch SE 3 remains the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience and can live without features such as ECG and the latest health sensors.
Apple updated the Series and Ultra models in September 2026, but the SE was unchanged. However, the SE 3 only arrived in 2025 and includes significant improvements over its predecessor, including an always-on display, temperature sensing and the same S10 chip found in the Series 11. You may also find older models at a discount, but check that the saving is worthwhile and bear in mind that watchOS 27 no longer supports every older Apple Watch. See our roundup of the best Apple Watch deals for the latest prices.
In this guide, we’ll explain the differences between the current models and help you decide whether you need to spend more on the Series 12 or Ultra 4 – or whether the SE 3 offers everything you need. We’ll compare their features, specifications and prices, as well as explain the choices of sizes, case materials, colors and bands, so you can buy the Apple Watch that best suits your needs.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s mainstream premium smartwatch and the best choice for most people. Its S11 chip powers a redesigned heart-rate sensor system that measures your heart rate every five seconds throughout the day. It also enables Audio Intelligence features including Sound Recognition, Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
The design remains familiar, but Apple has introduced new finishes: Light Gold and Dark Bronze replace Silver and Rose Gold on aluminum models, while Radiant Gold replaces Gold on titanium versions. Ceramic cases also return in Night Blue and Pearl White. Prices still start at $399, although some configurations cost more than their Series 11 equivalents.
Key advantages and limitations
Aluminum models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple claims is 60 percent more durable than the Ion-X glass used on the aluminum Series 11. Battery life remains at 24 hours, but outdoor workout tracking increases to 10 hours and the watch can charge to 80 percent in around 30 minutes.
Live Rewind can display a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of a conversation when you double-press the Digital Crown. However, assigning that gesture to Live Rewind means the traditional App Switcher is no longer available, making multitasking less convenient. The Series 12 also lacks the Ultra 4’s satellite connectivity, 50-hour battery life and brighter, more rugged display.
Who should buy the Apple Watch Series 12?
The Series 12 is the best option for anyone who wants Apple’s latest health and smart features without the size or price of the Ultra 4. Its advanced heart-rate sensing, Readiness score, tougher display and relatively compact design make it particularly attractive to health-conscious users and anyone upgrading from a Series 9 or older.
Who shouldn’t buy one?
Series 10 and 11 owners probably won’t gain enough to justify upgrading, especially because the quoted 24-hour battery life is unchanged. Outdoor adventurers who need satellite connectivity, extended workout tracking or maximum battery life should consider the Ultra 4 instead.
Should I buy an older version of the Apple Watch Series?
A discounted Series 10 or 11 could offer better value if you don’t need the new health sensing or Audio Intelligence features. The Series 9 is also still compatible with watchOS 27. Avoid the Series 8 and older models unless they are exceptionally cheap, because they cannot run watchOS 27 and will miss out on future feature updates.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is Apple’s most rugged and capable smartwatch, designed for endurance athletes and outdoor adventurers. It retains the Ultra 3’s 49mm titanium case, 3,000-nit display, Action button, dual-frequency GPS, satellite connectivity, 100-meter water resistance and recreational diving support.
Inside, the new S11 processor powers the redesigned heart-rate sensing system also found in the Series 12. It measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day and enables Audio Intelligence features including Sound Recognition, Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
Key advantages and limitations
Battery life is the Ultra 4’s biggest improvement, increasing from 42 to 50 hours under normal use. Extended Workout mode provides up to 25 hours with full GPS and heart-rate measurements, while Max Extended Workout mode can track outdoor runs and walks for up to 45 hours. Charging is faster too, with a 15-minute charge providing up to 18 hours of use.
Satellite connectivity, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving support and the bright display make it particularly well suited to demanding environments. However, its 49mm case is large and heavy, while charging to 80 percent takes around 45 minutes, compared with approximately 30 minutes for the Series 12. The external design is also largely unchanged. Pricing remains at $799, twice the Series 12’s starting price.
Who should buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4?
Choose the Ultra 4 if you need the longest Apple Watch battery life, highly accurate GPS, satellite connectivity, diving support or extended workout tracking. It is particularly suited to runners, hikers, cyclists, divers and anyone who regularly spends more than a day away from a charger.
Its extended battery life could also appeal to travelers and people working long shifts, even if they don’t participate in extreme sports.
Who shouldn’t buy one?
Most people will be better served by the smaller and less expensive Series 12. It provides the same S11 processor, redesigned heart-rate sensing and principal Audio Intelligence features without the Ultra’s bulk or $799 price. If you don’t need satellite communication, precision GPS, diving support or exceptionally long workout tracking, you are unlikely to benefit from the additional expense.
Should I buy an older Apple Watch Ultra?
The Ultra 3 remains a strong alternative if substantially discounted, although its battery lasts up to 42 rather than 50 hours. The Ultra 2 is the oldest model compatible with watchOS 27 and may also be worth considering at the right price, but it lacks some newer connectivity and battery improvements. Avoid the original Ultra unless it is exceptionally inexpensive, because it cannot run watchOS 27.

The Apple Watch SE 3 is Apple’s most affordable smartwatch and the best-value model in the current lineup. Introduced in September 2025, it brought substantial improvements over the SE 2, including an always-on display, the S10 processor used by the Series 11, temperature sensing, fast charging and 64GB of storage.
It also supports Double Tap and Wrist Flick gestures, on-device Siri and media playback through its speaker. The aluminum case comes in Midnight or Starlight, but there is no longer a Silver option. Prices start at $249/£219, although it can fall as low as $199 during sales.
Key advantages and limitations
The SE 3 provides the essential Apple Watch experience, including fitness and sleep tracking, Sleep Score, heart-rate alerts, temperature-based cycle tracking, Fall Detection and Crash Detection. Its Ion-X display glass is four times more crack-resistant than that of the SE 2, while cellular versions add 5G connectivity.
Battery life remains limited to 18 hours, although Low Power Mode extends this to 32 hours. Fast charging reaches approximately 80 percent in 45 minutes, and a 15-minute charge provides around eight hours of use. The SE 3 lacks ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring, hypertension notifications and the redesigned Health Sensing System found on the Series 12. Its 1,000-nit display, thicker bezels and limited material choices also make it feel less premium.
Who should buy the Apple Watch SE 3?
The SE 3 is ideal for first-time Apple Watch buyers and anyone who wants fitness tracking, notifications and safety features without paying for advanced health sensors. It is also a strong option for children when using the cellular model with Family Setup, and for older users who could benefit from Fall Detection, Emergency SOS and heart-rate monitoring.
Who shouldn’t buy one?
Choose the Series 12 instead if you want ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring, hypertension notifications, more advanced heart-rate sensing or a brighter, more premium display. Buyers who need multi-day battery life, satellite connectivity or specialist outdoor features should consider the Ultra 4.
Should I buy an older Apple Watch SE?
No. The SE 2 cannot run watchOS 27 and lacks the SE 3’s always-on display, temperature sensing, faster charging, newer gestures and additional storage. Even at a substantial discount, its reduced software lifespan makes it difficult to recommend in 2026.  

							
		


watchOS 27 features: What’s new and what requires Series 12 or Ultra 4
Apple released a new version of the software that runs on the Apple Watch – watchOS 27 – on September 14, 2026, but not every new feature is available on every supported watch. Some improvements are software-led and work across compatible models, while others depend on the S11 chip and redesigned sensors in the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
The hardware-dependent health features unique to the 2026 Watches include background heart-rate measurements every five seconds and HRV (heart rate variability) measurements every five minutes. The Series 12 and Ultra 4 also gain the Readiness app, which analyzes recent activity, training load, sleep and health data to produce a daily recovery score. Other exclusives include daytime resting heart-rate and HRV data in Vitals, a real-time chart in the Heart Rate app, more accurate all-day step counting and a Steps complication that updates on the watch face.
The S11 chip also enables Apple’s Audio Intelligence features. Automatic Music Recognition uses Shazam to identify nearby songs and display them in the Smart Stack, while Sound Recognition can detect doorbells, alarms, sirens and crying babies without relying on the iPhone. Live Rewind displays a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation after a double-press of the Digital Crown; it does not save an audio recording. Siri Recap produces high-level summaries of conversations. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are expected to arrive in beta later in 2026 and require a compatible Apple Intelligence iPhone and Siri AI.
Other watchOS 27 features are more widely available. These include the Dynamic App Grid, redesigned Find My app, menopause and perimenopause tracking, Call Context and Workout Buddy improvements. Apple has also introduced the Longevity section and Health Age.
Compatibility is considerably more restricted than it was with watchOS 26. Series 9 and Ultra 2 are now the oldest supported models, while the SE 3 is the only compatible SE. The Series 6, Series 7, Series 8, SE 2 and original Ultra cannot install watchOS 27. Anyone considering a discounted older Apple Watch should therefore choose a Series 9, Series 10, Series 11, Ultra 2 or Ultra 3 if receiving current feature updates is important. Choosing the right Apple Watch size depends on your wrist, how much display space you want and which model you prefer. Apple’s current lineup ranges from the compact 40mm Apple Watch SE 3 to the rugged 49mm Ultra 4.


ModelAvailable sizesCase dimensionsBest for

Apple Watch SE 340mm or 44mm40mm: 40 × 34 × 10.7mm; 44mm: 44 × 38 × 10.7mmSmaller wrists, lighter watches and budget-conscious buyers. The 40mm version is the smallest current Apple Watch.
Apple Watch Series 1242mm or 46mm42mm: 42 × 37 × 9.7mm; 46mm: 46 × 40 × 9.7mmThe best balance of display size and wearability for most people.
Apple Watch Ultra 449mm49 × 44 × 12mmAthletes and adventurers who want the largest display, most durable construction and longest battery life.

 



The Series 12 ceramic cases are slightly larger: approximately 43mm and 47mm rather than 42mm and 46mm.
Apple Watch Series 12 (46mm)
$549 at Amazon										 | 
										$549 at Best Buy US										 | 
										$549 at Walmart							
						



				
					

				
			
Foundry




Consider your wrist size and comfort
The watch should feel secure without dominating your wrist or restricting movement. The 40mm SE 3 is the best option for particularly small wrists, while the 42mm Series 12 provides a larger display in a case that remains manageable for most people. If possible, try both sizes in an Apple Store before buying.
Consider display size and readability
A larger screen makes text, notifications and onscreen controls easier to see and use. The 49mm Ultra 4 has the largest display, but its 63g titanium case is substantially heavier than the aluminum Series 12 or SE 3. The 46mm Series 12 offers a spacious display without the Ultra’s additional bulk.
Consider whether you need the Ultra
Don’t choose the Ultra 4 solely because it has the largest screen. Its size makes most sense if you also need its rugged titanium construction, satellite connectivity, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving support or 50-hour battery life. For everyday use, the Series 12 will generally be more comfortable.
Check band compatibility
Apple Watch bands aren’t universally interchangeable. Bands designed for smaller cases generally fit the 38mm, 40mm, 41mm and newer 42mm watches, while larger bands work with 44mm, 45mm, 46mm and 49mm models. However, the older 42mm case belongs to the larger band family, so check the compatibility information before reusing or ordering a band.


						

							


Aluminum, titanium or ceramic: Which Apple Watch material is best?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Another consideration when buying an Apple Watch is its case material, which affects its durability, weight, appearance and price. Apple currently offers aluminum, titanium and ceramic cases, although the available materials depend on the model.
Aluminum: Best for most people
Aluminum is the lightest and most affordable choice. It is the only material available for the Apple Watch SE 3 and the entry-level option for the Series 12, helping to keep their starting prices at $249 and $399 respectively.
It is a good choice for everyday wear, fitness and sleep tracking because it feels lighter on the wrist than the premium alternatives. The SE 3 uses Ion-X display glass, which Apple says is four times more crack-resistant than that of the SE 2. The aluminum Series 12 has the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 display, which Apple claims is 60 percent more durable than the Ion-X glass used by the aluminum Series 11.
Titanium: Best for premium durability
Titanium is available with the Series 12 and is the only case material offered with the Ultra 4. It provides a more premium finish and is paired with highly scratch-resistant sapphire crystal rather than the glass used on aluminum models.
The Series 12 titanium case is available in Natural or Radiant Gold. It is a good option for anyone who wants a more luxurious and durable everyday watch without moving up to the much larger Ultra.
The Ultra 4 uses a rugged Grade 5 titanium case in Natural or Black. It is designed for outdoor adventures, endurance sports and diving, with a 49mm case, 100-meter water resistance and recreational diving support. However, its size and 63g weight make it less comfortable for smaller wrists and sleep tracking.
Ceramic: Best for distinctive styling
Ceramic returns as a premium Series 12 option in Pearl White and Night Blue. It has a glossy, distinctive finish and uses a sapphire crystal display, but it is heavier and considerably more expensive than the aluminum version. The ceramic cases are also slightly larger than the other Series 12 configurations.
Which material is best for Apple Watch?
For most buyers, aluminum offers the best balance of price, durability and comfort. Choose titanium if you want a more premium finish, sapphire crystal or the Ultra 4’s specialized outdoor capabilities. Ceramic is primarily a style-led luxury choice for buyers who want the most distinctive Series 12 and are prepared to pay more for it.


						

							




Which Apple Watch strap should you choose?

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The right Apple Watch strap depends on how you intend to use your watch. Apple offers options for everyday wear, sleep tracking, exercise, water sports and formal occasions, while third-party manufacturers provide an even wider range of styles and prices.


StrapBest forKey characteristics

Sport BandEveryday wear, workouts and swimmingDurable rubber with a secure pin-and-tuck closure. Water and sweat resistant, but less breathable than fabric.
Sport LoopSleep tracking and all-day comfortSoft, lightweight and breathable nylon with an adjustable hook-and-loop fastener.
Nike Sport BandRunning and intense workoutsSimilar to the Sport Band but perforated for improved ventilation.
Nike Sport LoopRunning and everyday wearA breathable fabric alternative to the Nike Sport Band.
Solo LoopEveryday wear and sleepStretchable silicone with no clasp or buckle. Comfortable, but choosing the correct size is essential.
Braided Solo LoopComfort with a smarter finishA stretchable woven band that feels more premium than the standard Solo Loop.
Alpine LoopHiking and outdoor adventuresDurable double-layer textile with a secure titanium G-hook. Designed for the Apple Watch Ultra.

Ocean BandSwimming, diving and water sportsWater-resistant elastomer with a corrosion-resistant titanium buckle.

Link BraceletFormal and premium wearApple’s premium metal bracelet, with removable links for adjusting the fit.
Modern Buckle or Magnetic LinkSmart everyday wearMore formal alternatives to the sport-focused straps, available for selected case sizes.
Hermès strapsLuxury and fashionPremium woven, rubber and metal designs made in collaboration with Hermès.

 



For most people, the Sport Loop is the best all-round choice because it is light, breathable and easy to adjust. Its softness also makes it particularly comfortable for sleep tracking.
For workouts and swimming, choose a Sport Band or Nike Sport Band. The perforated Nike version provides better ventilation during intense exercise. Divers and regular swimmers should consider the Ocean Band, while runners and hikers may prefer the lighter Trail Loop or more rugged Alpine Loop.
For work or formal occasions, the Milanese Loop, Link Bracelet, Modern Buckle and Magnetic Link provide a smarter appearance. Apple’s Hermès collection offers the most luxurious—and most expensive—options.
Before buying, check that the strap supports your Apple Watch case size and wrist measurement. Solo Loop and Braided Solo Loop straps require particularly careful sizing because they cannot be adjusted with a clasp. Third-party straps can offer excellent value, but quality, fit and fastening security vary considerably.


Do I need a cellular Apple Watch?
Whether you need a cellular Apple Watch depends mainly on how often you plan to leave your iPhone behind. For most buyers, the answer is no: a GPS-only Apple Watch offers better value and can already do a great deal without an active connection to an iPhone.
Away from your iPhone, a GPS Apple Watch can still track workouts, monitor health, record location data, use Apple Pay and play music or podcasts downloaded to the watch. When connected to a known Wi-Fi network, it can also send and receive messages, make calls and use many online services. See our guide to Everything an Apple Watch can do without an iPhone.
Cellular becomes useful when you regularly leave your iPhone at home but still want calls, messages, music streaming, navigation and notifications. This makes it particularly valuable for runners, cyclists, swimmers and gym users who don’t want to carry a phone. It can also provide reassurance when you are walking alone or exercising away from Wi-Fi, because the watch can contact emergency services after a fall or crash using its own mobile connection.
A cellular model is also the right choice when setting up an Apple Watch for a child or older relative who doesn’t have an iPhone. Apple Watch For Your Kids, previously called Family Setup, allows a family member’s watch to be configured from another person’s iPhone. A cellular plan enables calls, messages and location sharing when the watch is away from the managing iPhone.
The drawbacks are cost and redundancy. A cellular Series or SE generally costs more than its GPS equivalent, and you must also pay your network provider a monthly fee. If your iPhone is nearly always in your pocket or bag, the watch will normally use its connection instead, leaving you paying for cellular service that you rarely need. See: I switched to a cellular Apple Watch to prove I didn’t need one.
Our recommendation: The Ultra 4 includes cellular as standard, so there is no GPS-only version. For the Series 12 and SE 3, choose cellular only if you expect to leave your iPhone behind regularly or need Family Setup. Otherwise, save your money and buy the GPS model. For a more detailed comparison, see The pros and cons of a cellular Apple Watch.


						

							


Can you use an Apple Watch without an iPhone?
Yes, but with important caveats. An Apple Watch can do a surprising amount without an iPhone nearby, but an iPhone is required for the initial setup and to manage some settings. You cannot set up an Apple Watch using a Mac, iPad or Android phone.
The exception is Apple Watch For Your Kids, previously called Family Setup. This allows a parent or guardian to use their iPhone to configure a cellular Apple Watch for a child or another family member who doesn’t have an iPhone of their own.
Once it has been set up, an Apple Watch can perform many tasks without its paired iPhone nearby – and some don’t require an internet connection at all. These include:
Tracking workouts and activity: Record runs, walks and other exercises, close Activity rings and collect GPS data. The results sync with the iPhone when it reconnects.
Monitoring health: Measure heart rate, track sleep, log medications and use other health features supported by the particular watch.
Playing downloaded media: Listen to music, podcasts and audiobooks stored on the watch using Bluetooth headphones.
Using Apple Pay: Make contactless payments without an iPhone or internet connection once Apple Pay has been configured.
Using offline tools: Set alarms and timers, use the stopwatch and compass, and view photos that have been synced to the watch.
Other features require either Wi-Fi or a cellular connection when the iPhone isn’t nearby. With an internet connection, the watch can make and receive calls, send messages, check email, stream music and podcasts, use Maps and access online apps and services.
Fall Detection and Crash Detection can still recognize an incident without the iPhone, but the watch requires Wi-Fi or its own cellular connection to contact emergency services. This is an important consideration if you are buying an Apple Watch for an older relative or someone who may regularly be away from their phone.
An Apple Watch therefore cannot completely replace an iPhone, but it doesn’t need to remain beside it throughout the day. For a complete breakdown, read all the things an Apple Watch can do without an iPhone.


						

							


How we choose the best Apple Watch
Macworld’s Apple Watch recommendations draw on more than a decade of hands-on experience. Our writers have tested and reviewed every generation since the original Apple Watch, comparing each new model with both its current rivals and previous generations before deciding whether it deserves a recommendation.
Our assessment focuses on the factors that make a meaningful difference in everyday use:
Real-world testing: We assess comfort, build quality, display visibility, performance, battery life, charging, health sensors, fitness tracking and software features. We also consider how well the watch performs during everyday activities, workouts and sleep tracking—not simply how its specifications compare on paper.
Value and upgrade potential: A newer or more expensive Apple Watch is not automatically the best choice. We consider whether its improvements justify the price, whether owners of recent models would benefit from upgrading and whether a discounted previous-generation watch offers better value.
Honest recommendations: We clearly identify compromises such as limited battery life, missing health sensors, a bulky design or features that most people are unlikely to use. We don’t recommend a product simply because it has the most impressive specifications.
Advice for different buyers: There is no single Apple Watch that suits everyone. We recommend the Series 12 for most buyers, the SE 3 for those seeking the best value, and the Ultra 4 for endurance athletes and outdoor adventurers who need its longer battery life, rugged construction and specialist capabilities.
Our final recommendations therefore combine extensive testing, expert judgment, price analysis and practical buying advice. The aim is not merely to identify the Apple Watch with the longest feature list, but to help you find the model that provides the right balance of features, comfort and value for the way you will actually use it.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Is now a good time to buy an Apple Watch
Yes. Now is a great time to buy an Apple Watch because the brand-new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 went on sale on September 18, 2026 and none of the line up is likely to be updated until September 2027. See: Should I buy an Apple Watch now or wait? 





2.
What is the difference between the Series 12 and SE 3?
The Apple Watch Series 12 offers a brighter, tougher display, premium aluminum, titanium and ceramic cases, and the newer S11 chip. It also includes advanced health features such as ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring, high-frequency heart-rate sensing and the Readiness app, plus exclusive Audio Intelligence features. Battery life is rated at 24 hours. 
The $249/£219 SE 3 uses the S10 chip, lasts 18 hours and provides essential fitness, sleep and safety features, but lacks the Series 12’s advanced sensors and premium materials.





3.
Can you swim while wearing an Apple Watch?
Yes, you can swim while wearing an Apple Watch, but the level of water resistance varies significantly depending on the model. The Apple Watch Ultra models are the most water-capable in the lineup. They are water-resistant to 100 meters and are suitable for swimming, snorkeling, scuba diving (up to 40 meters), and high-speed water sports. The Ultra models also include a depth gauge (up to 40 meters) and a water temperature sensor, making them a genuine companion for divers and endurance swimmers. 
The standard Apple Watch Series 11 and Series 10 are water-resistant to 50 meters and are described as “swimproof”. They are perfectly safe for swimming in a pool or the ocean, as well as for snorkeling and casual diving down to about 6 meters.
The Apple Watch SE 3 is also water-resistant to 50 meters and is considered “swimproof”.
To prepare your Watch before swimming by swiping up to open Control Center and tapping the water drop icon to enable Water Lock mode to prevent accidental screen taps. After your swim, turn the Digital Crown to eject any water from the speaker.

title: iPhone 18 Pro is the same size as the 17 Pro, right? That’s not quite the case
content:
Macworld





Apple’s latest iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max look identical to the previous iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max generation, with a few minor visual differences such as a smaller Dynamic Island at the front and, of course, the new colors (RIP Cosmic Orange). The brushed aluminum unibody chassis and camera plateau are practically identical, and according to Apple’s tech specs, they have the exact same measurements:
iPhone 17 Pro dimensions
Height: 5.91 inches (150mm)
Width: 2.83 inches (71.9mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 18 Pro dimensions
Height: 5.91 inches (150mm)
Width: 2.83 inches (71.9mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 17 Pro Max dimensions
Height: 6.43 inches (163.4mm)
Width: 3.07 inches (78mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 18 Pro Max dimensions
Height: 6.43 inches (163.4mm)
Width: 3.07 inches (78mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
The iPhone 18 Pro is slightly heavier, weighing 211g versus the iPhone 17 Pro’s 204g; Pro Max 249g vs 233g, but that’s the result of what’s inside: the new A20 Pro chip, Apple cellular modems, and a new vapour chamber. So it would seem that any iPhone 17 Pro case would be compatible with the newest phones. That might not be the case (no pun intended).

				
					

				
			
TORRAS




Will an iPhone 18 Pro fit in a case for an iPhone 17 Pro?
Even though the 18 Pro and 17 Pro phones have the same dimensions, there’s a barely perceptible physical difference: The camera bump on the iPhone 18 Pro/Max is about 0.5mm taller than on the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. That’s not an iPhone 18 Pro measurement that Apple tracks in its tech specs.
So while you’d expect that the iPhone 18 Pro can fit in a case made for the iPhone 17 Pro, some might fit a little too snugly or look a little off, much like if you put an iPhone 16 Pro in an iPhone 17 Pro case (which also kind of works). It varies by brand and case type.
In the course of our testing of new cases for the iPhone 18 Pro series, we found numerous case makers that list 17 Pro/18 Pro compatibility. When we reached out for clarification, leading case manufacturer OtterBox told Macworld that its iPhone 18 Pro/Max cases are “also compatible with iPhone 17 Pro, so the cases can be used interchangeably between those two models.”
Similarly, Decoded told us that all its iPhone 18 cases “are also compatible with the iPhone 17 models.” Mous acknowledged that while “the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max lineup has a taller camera bump, our iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max cases will also fit” the 18, but noted that its new cases “are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection”.
However, several case makers disagreed on the case compatibility between 17 and 18 iPhones. In particular, cases designed with tight tolerances might therefore have a problem with the 18’s taller camera bump.
For example, Rokform, which specializes in rugged cases, told Macworld that any iPhone 18 Pro case will be compatible with both iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro models. However, its older iPhone 17 Pro case lineup is not compatible with iPhone 18 models due to camera plateau design differences. 
So, the bottom line is this: You should be able to fit a 17 Pro/Max in a new case designed for the 18 Pro/Max, but the opposite might not be true. So if you’re shopping for a new case for your new iPhone 18 Pro, make sure you get one that specifcally says it’s compatible with the iPhone 18 Pro. 
New cases are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection, so buying a case built specifically for your iPhone model is always the safest option: see our roundup of the best cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max and best cases for iPhone 17.

title: iPhone batteries compared: Capacity, mAh and watt hours for every iPhone
content:
Macworld





Battery life is one of the most important factors when choosing which iPhone to buy. 
Measuring iPhone battery life in straight hours of real-world usage (as Apple likes to do) is not an accurate metric for comparison purposes as so many use and environmental factors play a part.
Here at Macworld we run our own battery life tests, which should give you a more accurate representation of how long the battery in your iPhone will last. In the table below you can see battery life (in minutes). 
Another way to gauge battery life is to look at the technical specifications to find out the battery capacities of each iPhone. Unfortunately, Apple is notoriously secretive about these battery specifications, mainly because smartphones from rivals such as Samsung boast much larger battery capacities. The only way to discover the battery capacities is by ripping the battery out of the phone and checking the specifications printed there.
Below you will find a list and explanation of the battery capacities of every iPhone from 2007’s original iPhone to the very latest iPhone 18 series, including the iPhone Air and Duo. The Duo capacity is estimated and we’ll update when we know for sure after its release.
iPhone battery life tests
This chart shows that there is a clear and impressive increase in battery life over time. Battery capacity has grown significantly, doubling from the iPhone 8 to the iPhone 17, and going even further in the latest Pro and Pro Max iPhones. But battery life has extended much more than that, with the iPhone 17 running the same test, at the same brightness, lasting over five times as long as the iPhone 8! Bear in mind that screen size has increased quite a bit over this time, too.
For more details about our battery life tests of every iPhone from the iPhone X to the iPhone 16 Pro Max see: How much the iPhone’s battery life has improved.
iPhone mAh and Wh: what’s the difference?
We can look at the straight technical specifications to find out the battery capacities of each iPhone, but as mentioned above, to do so requires opening up the iPhone to see the details on the battery itself. 
Battery capacity is measured in either Milliamp Hours (mAh) or Watt Hours (Wh).
Milliamp hours are a measure of electrical charge, while a watt-hour is equal to one watt of energy consumed for one hour of time. And it is the energy consumed that matters when we’re measuring actual battery life.
Learn how to properly charge a phone battery.
Wh is a more accurate and consistent way to compare the total amount of energy that similar types of batteries can store.
And it’s all about the battery voltage, which mAh ignores, which determines the wattage (power) of a battery.
If the mAh is the same, the higher the voltage, the greater the actual stored power.
Volts (V) are a measure of electric pressure. Amps (A) are a measure of current. Multiply V x A and you get Watts (W) that are a measure of power. So V × A = W.
You can convert watt hours (Wh) to milliamp hours (mAh) using this formula: (Wh x 1,000) divided by V = mAh.
The lithium batteries that power most portable electronics have a voltage of about 3.6V, but some external battery packs (such as Apple’s 7.62V MagSafe Battery Pack) boast a higher voltage, which means they actually carry more power than their mAh implies.

title: Fan Site Lets You 'Design the Next iPhone'
content:
"Design the Next iPhone," an interactive website from developer Neal Agarwal, gives users control over a virtual iPhone's look, including the option to combine conventional smartphone components with deliberately impractical accessories.


The interactive tool starts with a bare iPhone model that can be rotated in 3D, with users able to drag and drop components onto its surface. Cameras, volume buttons, Lightning ports, Home buttons, and Apple logos can be placed wherever users want, with multiple copies of each item available for more unconventional designs.

Beyond standard smartphone features, the site offers a headphone jack, HDMI port, Apple Watch-style Digital Crown, and a hinge. Users can also add an Android or pear logo, a rotary dial, an antenna, or a classic iPod click wheel. The more absurd options include a steering wheel, a joystick, and a Mac Pro "Pro Wheel." 

Tim Cook praising the design. The finished iPhone can be downloaded as a rotating video.

title: Do You Really Need a Bulky Phone Case for Serious Protection?
content:
Macworld





		
Meet the New Era of Protection
Less Bulk. More Freedom.
View Ostand Q3 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are, by most accounts, some of the best-looking iPhones Apple has ever made. Which makes it a little painful that the first thing most of us do after buying one is bury it inside a case. 
That’s the compromise that’s defined phone accessories for years: you either protect your investment or you enjoy the design you paid for, but rarely both. A case substantial enough to survive a concrete sidewalk tends to turn a sleek slab of titanium and glass into something closer to a brick. A case slim enough to preserve that in-hand feel often leaves you one bad drop away from a cracked screen and an expensive repair.

				
					

				
			
Torras




TORRAS’s answer, with its new Ostand Q3 lineup, is that this trade-off is increasingly outdated. Smarter materials and more deliberate engineering mean a case doesn’t need bulk to do serious protective work—and it can pull double duty as a stand, a grip, and a mount while it’s at it. The Ostand Q3 Air Pro and Ostand Q3 Rugged are built on that premise, and they take slightly different routes to it.

				
					

				
			
Torras




Q3 Air Pro: Protection Without the Padding
The Q3 Air Pro is Torras’s showcase for what it calls Air² Pro Tech, a sealed dual-layer airbag system called Air Duet that it describes as the first of its kind, borrowing an idea from performance sneakers: rather than relying on sheer mass to blunt an impact, staged internal air chambers absorb and dissipate force before it reaches the phone.
The result is a case rated for drops of up to 16 feet, while measuring just 2.5mm at the sides and weighing 53g for the iPhone 18 Pro (61g for the Pro Max). Raised edges around the screen and camera add targeted reinforcement, anti-slip side texture improves grip, and a microfiber lining protects the phone’s finish from the inside.
It’s the case for someone who wants real drop protection but refuses to give up the phone’s actual shape.
Q3 Rugged: The Traditional Approach, Trimmed Down
The Q3 Rugged leans on more familiar rugged-case construction—a polycarbonate backplate wrapped in a TPU frame, with air-cushion protection built into the top and bottom edges and raised lips guarding the screen and camera. The best protection, of course, is not dropping your phone in the first place, so the Q3 Rugged includes additional grip along the sides to make the phone easier to hold while moving or working out.
It’s the more conventional route to durability, but Torras has kept the bulk in check: 47g for the iPhone 18 Pro and 59g for the Pro Max, with a matte, precision-textured grip that’s clearly aimed at commutes, workouts, and anything more physical than a desk job.
It’s also MagSafe compatible, and more affordable at $49.99–$51.99 against the Q3 Air Pro’s $79.99.

				
					

				
			
Torras




Ostand Gives the Cases Extra Functions
What ties the two together is Torras’s 3-in-1 Ostand, a rotating ring built into the back of each case rather than bolted on as an afterthought.
It rotates a full 360° horizontally and opens up to 180° vertically, which gives it three practical modes: Stand, for propping the phone up to watch video, join a call, or follow a recipe hands-free; Hang, for suspending the phone somewhere useful when there’s no flat surface nearby, like a gym rack; and Snap, which uses the case’s magnetic connection — 18N of holding force on the Q3 Air Pro — to attach wallets, power banks, or car and bike mounts.
So, Do You Need the Bulk?
Not anymore, really. Between a sophisticated airbag system and a leaner take on rugged construction, TORRAS’s Ostand Q3 lineup makes a reasonable case that “slim” and “seriously protected” don’t have to be opposing goals.

title: Your iPhone’s USB-C port can do a lot more than fast-charge
content:
Macworld





If you’re upgrading to the iPhone 18 Pro from an iPhonr 14 Pro or earlier, you’ll notice that it has a USB-C port. In fact, all iPhone and iPad models now use USB-C, including the low-end 17e, but you might not know that it can do a whole lot more than just charge. USB-C opens up a range of options that Lightning couldn’t do, from powering monitors to charging your AIrPods. Read on to see what your new iPhone’s tiny port can do.


1. Charge another device
Rival companies, like Samsung, have long supported reverse wireless charging, letting users turn their smartphones into portable Qi pads. However, it’s not all that practical, forcing users to flip over their phones and rendering both unusable. With the iPhone 15 and newer models, Apple introduced its own version that works via the USB-C port.
Your iPhone can now deliver up to 4.5W of power, letting you charge your AirPods, Apple Watch, or even a friend’s Android phone. To do so, simply plug your USB-C cable into the iPhone and the other end into the USB-C port on the other device.


						

							


2. Increase your storage
Even with 128 GB as the standard, we’ve probably all come across the iPhone’s full storage alert. While data stored in iCloud can easily be offloaded from the local memory, not all users trust cloud storage. Fortunately, the iPhone supports a wide range of external storage devices, including USB sticks and hard drives. This makes it easy to free up space by moving large files to a separate drive. To get started, connect a compatible flash drive to your iPhone using its USB-C port. You can then view, manage, and transfer data using the built-in Files app.
One of the solid options out there is this tiny Samsung Type-C Flash Drive ($80), which supports regular file transfers and real-time ProRes video storage. As a Pro exclusive, those with the highest-end iPhone models can directly record ProRes video to a compatible external storage device. Given the considerable size of raw footage, being able to write the data directly onto a separate device can help you shoot for longer periods and avoid filling up your iPhone’s memory.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone’s USB-C cable can do more than just charge your iPhone.

Foundry



							


3. Connect a keyboard
While iPads and Macs are better suited for long-form typing, iPhones—especially the near-7-inch Plus and Pro Max models—can still handle productivity tasks effectively. To make the most of the relatively small screen, though, you may want to pair it with a dedicated keyboard. Fortunately, iOS natively supports this through the USB-C port.
Most standard keyboards, such as this compact Macally keyboard ($30), will work with your iPhone just fine. See our roundup of the best Mac keyboards. Or if you want to always have a keyboard with you, you can opt for a Clicks case ($139), which connects to your USB-C port so it’s always ready for a text or email. 


						

							


4. Amplify your microphone
In the era of TikTok, everyone is a content creator, so a high-quality microphone is an essential tool. Fortunately, your iPhone’s USB-C port can support a wide range of them, letting you pair your footage with crystal-clear high-quality audio. One reliable option is the Rode Wireless Micro ($85), which utilizes your iPhone’s port while maintaining the convenience of wireless recording.


						

							


5. Add an SD card
Photographers and videographers love the handy SD card slots on board the newest MacBook Pro and Mac Studio, but that convenience doesn’t extend to the device that does most of your shooting. Fortunately, that can be easily remedied with a wired SD card reader. While newer cameras generally support wireless photo transfers via their respective companion apps, the process tends to be slower than the wired alternative. Apple’s USB-C to SD Card Reader ($39) connects to your iPhone through its charging port and should work with all relevant SD cards. You can also use this same dongle with your Mac or iPad when editing on a larger screen. See more of the best USB-C adapters.


						

							


6. Hook up an external display
If you’re staying at a hotel that blocks wireless media casting, you may be able to mirror your iPhone’s screen to the TV using a wired solution. Apple’s USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter ($69) transforms your iPhone’s charging port into an HDMI connector, allowing you to watch 4K content on bigger displays using a regular HDMI cable.
Check out our roundups of the best monitors and best portable monitors.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone can connect to most displays with a single cable.

Foundry



							


7. Plug in a game controller
Thanks to the A17 and A18 chips, the latest Pro-tier iPhones can run some AAA games. Notably, though, these titles typically need a controller, as touch controls don’t always offer the best gameplay, if they’re available at all. While Sony’s DualSense controller ($75) supports Bluetooth pairing, opting for wired mode using the iPhone’s USB-C port can minimize latency and enhance overall performance.


						

							


8. Connect to Ethernet 
Speaking of gaming, the iPhone fully supports Ethernet dongles, allowing for faster download and upload speeds. While Wi-Fi and 5G are sufficient for most users, Ethernet can come in handy when seeking an even more dependable connection. Belkin’s USB-C to Ethernet Adapter ($23) is one of the solid options that is guaranteed to get the job done.


						

							


9. Peer into small places
There are many accessories that you can plug into your iPhone’s USB-C port, but none are cooler than a borescope/endoscope camera. Basically, it’s a snake wire with a tiny HD endoscope camera at the end and an LCD light. It’s flexible yet rigid enough to fit into the smallest of crevices, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without it. We haven’t tested them, but this model has a 4.3-star rating with nearly 7,000 reviews and costs just $30.

				
					

				
			
You can attach a tiny USB-C camera to your iPhone’s USB-C port to see into small places.

Amazon



							


10. Cool off in summer
With temperatures steadily rising all around the world, we can all use a little relief during long days outdoors. Your iPhone’s USB-C port can help there too. This 17,000 RPM ,4-setting high-speed fan ($15) plugs directly into your iPhone’s USB-C port and offers a “focused airflow channel that generates a high-speed airflow of up to 36 ft/s.” Reviewers praise its size, portability, and low-power requirements, but you’ll just appreciate a quick blast of cool air when you’re overheating.


						

							


11. Plug and don’t play
When you’re not using your iPhone’s USB-C port, it’s just a gaping hole at the bottom of your phone waiting to collect dust, dirt, and lint. A USB-C plug will make sure your port stays clean and clear for as long as you use your iPhone. You can get a bunch of them ($7) for just a few bucks, or you can get one that sticks to the back of your phone ($8), so you don’t keep losing them. An added bonus: it doubles as a handy pinky rest when you’re using your iPhone with one hand.
Read further: How to stop dust, dirt, and lint from getting into your iPhone charging port.


						

							


12. Talk to your car
Apple introduced wireless CarPlay a few years ago, but if you don’t have a newer car, you’ll still need to plug into your car’s USB port. For that, you’ll need a USB cable that supports data and charging, and one that’s long enough to reach wherever your car’s USB-C port is, and flexible enough not to get caught on any knobs or vents. A coiled USB-C cable is perfect for such instances, such as these popular Chubby Cable car-charging cables that come in USB-C-to-USB-C and USB-C-to-USB-A options for $20, as well as a variety of colors. 
Read further: Best magnetic wireless and USB car chargers and mounts for iPhone.


						

							


One port can do it all
The biggest detriment of the iPhone is that there’s just one port, but a USB hub can give you much more. We recommend the Plugable 7-in-1 USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter ($40), which will bring a headphone jack, USB-C charging, HDMI, an SD card reader, Ethernet, and even a couple of USB-A ports for good measure. It’s not exactly small, but if you need to use several ports at once, there’s no substitute.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone’s USB-C port is a multi-purpose connector for displays, hard drives, and other accessories.

Connor Jewiss / Foundry




Michael Simon contributed to this report.

title: If you multitask on your Apple Watch, don’t upgrade to watchOS 27
content:
Macworld





Whether you’re buying a new Series 12 or upgrading a Series 11 to watchOS 27, some big changes are coming to your Apple Watch. Apple Intelligence will have a prominent role on Apple’s wearable device for the first time, with a new Siri AI app and several Audio Intelligence features on the latest models.
One of those features, Live Rewind, records everything that you hear in 15-second intervals that can be accessed by double-pressing the Digital Crown. Current Apple Watch users will recognize that same action is used to open the App Switcher, which is used to quickly jump back to a previously used app. And if you turn on “Auto-Select Focused App” in Accessibility, you don’t even have to tap the screen.
If you buy a new Apple Watch, that option is gone. In fact, the App Switcher doesn’t even exist. That also means the option to swipe left to quickly close an app is gone, too. Instead, you’ll need to fumble through a clunky series of steps: Open the app, hold the side button until the emergency sliders appear, release the button, then press and hold the Digital Crown until your watch face appears.
However, if you download watchOS 27 on an older watch, you’ll also lose the double-click action even though those watches don’t have Live Rewind. Effectively, it does nothing. Double-pressing the button brings up the new Dynamic App Grid, but so does a single press.
The Dynamic App Grid is similar to the App Switcher in that it shows your recently used apps, but you still need to select the one you want to open. So multitasking is much less efficient.
Of course, this only applies to the Apple Watch Series 9 and later. Apple dropped compatibility for several models with this latest release, and there’s no indication that the Dynamic App Grid will come to older models.
